batching: 10 items per call, 12 calls per labeller, items in corpus order

labellers.output_instruction_suffix:
---
Task: apply the guide above to the items the user sends. Reply with ONLY a JSON array, one object per item, in the given order: {"id":..., "label":...} plus "coded_label" for ifhas-screen items. Use exact label strings from section 2 for the item's kind. No commentary, no code fences.
labellers.user_message: json.dumps(batch_of_10_items, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), items exactly as in the labeller input file

labellers.output_instruction_suffix: Output format: reply with ONLY a JSON array, no prose, no code fences. One object per item given, in order: {"id":...,"label":...} and, for ifhas-screen items only, also "coded_label". Use exact label strings from the guide.
labellers.prefix: You are a blind labeller. Follow the labelling guide below exactly.
labellers.user_message: 'Label these items:\n' + json.dumps(batch_of_10_items restricted to id, kind, programme, text, coded, ensure_ascii=False)

limitations: The prompt texts were reconstructed from the committed guide plus the stored prefix/suffix text; the reconstructed prompt hashes match the recorded hashes (tested), but the transcripts of the model calls were not archived.
The labelling ran in a sibling-branch workspace; the committed copy is evidence of what the input contained, not a recording of the API requests.
Both labellers were reached through the same LiteLLM gateway.
relation_to_canonical_corpus: The 120 items (id, programme, kind, text, coded) are identical to data/fresh2/corpus.json items; the canonical corpus additionally carries item_metadata and provenance, which the labellers did not see. The file sha256 differs from the canonical corpus sha256 because of the removed blocks and different JSON formatting; the label files bind to the canonical sha256.
statement: data/fresh2/labeller-input.json is the item source that was supplied to both labellers (declaration_exact_input_supplied). The committed file is a byte copy of out/fresh2-blind/corpus.json from the sibling-branch workspace where the labelling was run; that input is metadata-free and contains only the 120 items with the fields id, programme, kind, text and (ifhas-screen only) coded, plus the top-level schema field, with no item_metadata, no provenance block, no author key and no label. File timestamps are not evidence of the supplied input. The original sibling-workspace file was not committed on this branch, and the prompt texts were reconstructed from the committed guide and the stored prefix/suffix text rather than archived from the calls.
